pill.desc: clear, colorless solution in a single-dose glass vial

clues.kinetics: Metabolized by exonuclease hydrolysis rather than CYP450 enzymes, and not an inhibitor or inducer of them. Urinary excretion is the likely route, but only 0.5% of the dose is recovered in urine at 24 hours.
clues.substance: Supplied as the sodium salt, with 2.4 mg of active moiety per mL equivalent to 2.53 mg of the salt.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in 12, 28 and 50 mg single-dose vials, given every 14 days at first and then every 4 months.
clues.safety: No boxed warning and no contraindications. Lower respiratory infection and constipation are the most common adverse reactions.
clues.indication: Spinal muscular atrophy in pediatric and adult patients.
clues.mechanism: Directed at SMN2, it increases exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 transcripts, raising production of full-length SMN protein.

tell: An intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide with a plasma half-life of 63 to 87 days and maintenance doses every 4 months.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Median plasma Tmax values ranged from 1.7 to 6.0 hours
